text: Meridian Finworks' three-lesson capstone pulled on every chapter of this course, not just the ones it most obviously touches. This review walks through what each chapter actually contributed, as a decision you watched play out, before closing out Azure and AWS Cloud Security Engineering for good.

Chapter 1's shared responsibility model and CSPM vocabulary meant Lesson 29 could open with a flagged finding and already know whose job it was to fix. Chapter 2's Conditional Access and service principal lessons became Lesson 29's hardening policy and Lesson 30's accountEnabled remediation. Chapter 3's IAM policies and Access Analyzer ran through the hardening lab, the credential compromise, and Lesson 31's case study alike.

Chapter 4 is why NSGs and Security Groups in Lesson 29 read as the same idea in two syntaxes, not two systems to learn separately. Chapter 5's Defender for Cloud and GuardDuty coverage is exactly what surfaced Lesson 31's over-broad role through a routine posture finding, not a planned audit. Chapter 6's Key Vault and KMS are where Lesson 30's rotated secrets belonged once each incident closed.

Chapter 7 is the backbone of Lesson 30 end to end: the enumerate-escalate-persist-act sequence, Activity Log and CloudTrail reading skills, and the containment-before-full-certainty principle all showed up directly, on both the Azure and AWS sides of that simulated compromise.

Across three lessons, Meridian hardened identity and network together on two clouds, detected and contained a dual-cloud credential compromise using each cloud's own log source, and uncovered a misconfigured role whose scope -- not just its permissions -- had quietly set the blast radius for a future incident. That is the real job: recognizing identity, network, and detection as the same problems, solved twice, in two clouds' native tools.

Azure and AWS Cloud Security Engineering is now complete. The Advanced Specialization stage of the Cybersecurity Analyst to Security Engineer path continues with Python Security Automation, SOAR and DevSecOps -- scripting the exact detection and containment steps this chapter just walked through by hand.
